newsitem.title: CANADA: Hydro-Quebec buys stake in natural gas firm.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec buys stake in natural gas firm.

text.p: Hydro-Quebec said Monday it acquired a 40 percent interest in natural gas holding company Noverco Inc. in a C$309 million ($229 million) deal.
Hydro-Quebec, the Quebec government-owned electrical utility, bought the stake from the Caisse de depot et placement du Quebec, the Canadian province's public pension fund manager.
The acquisition was part of a two-tiered transaction in which SOQUIP, a Quebec government energy agency, sold its 38 percent interest in Noverco to the Caisse for C$291.5 million ($216 million).
The Hydro-Quebec deal made it the largest shareholder in Noverco with a 40 percent stake, followed by the Caisse at 36 percent and Gaz de France with 24 percent.
Noverco is a holding company that owns 100 percent of Gaz Metropolitain Inc., Quebec's natural gas distributor. Gaz Metropolitain also owns Northern New England Gas Corp. and Vermont Gas Systems Inc.
Hydro-Quebec said its stake includes 32 percent of Noverco's common shares and an option to buy an 8 percent block of shares held by brokerage Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion Inc.

Hydro-Quebec said the electrical utility and Gaz Metropolitain would remain separate corporate entities. They would, however, combine efforts to increase their penetration of the North American energy market.

Thierry Vandal, vice-president of planning and development at Hydro-Quebec, told a news conference that the utility was seeking to increase its 3 percent to 4 percent share of the $200 billion North American energy market.

He said Quebec was following the North American trend toward opening its energy markets to other suppliers. Late last year, Hydro-Quebec opened its network to allow private and public suppliers from Quebec and elsewhere to transport electricity through the province to other markets.

Hydro-Quebec generates and distributes most of the electricity produced in the province, but the utility could eventually open its power grid to retail suppliers from outside the province on a reciprocal basis, Vandal said.
Vandal compared Hydro-Quebec's partnership with Noverco to the recently proposed merger of Brooklyn Union Gas Co. and Long Island Lighting Co.
"These partnerships are part of the required steps toward a fully open and competitive marketplace and we are going to be a major player in that marketplace," Vandal said.
